sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Define 'Still Life' in visual arts and give two common examples of objects used in such drawings. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Still life is an artwork depicting inanimate, everyday objects arranged together on a surface. Common examples include a bowl of fresh fruit or a flower vase.

questions.question_text: What is the role of a 'Raga' in creating emotions during a musical performance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Raga provides a specific melodic framework of notes that musicians use to evoke distinct moods, atmospheres, or deep emotional responses from the listening audience.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the basic process of making a simple block print using everyday materials like potatoes. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: You cut a potato in half, carve a raised design into the flat surface, apply wet paint or ink to the design, and firmly press it onto paper.

questions.question_text: Why is 'proportion' an important principle when drawing a human figure or face? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Proportion ensures that different body parts and facial features are correctly sized relative to one another, making the final drawing look realistic, balanced, and visually accurate.

questions.question_text: Name two distinct types of traditional Indian musical instruments and mention how they produce sound. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Tabla produces rhythmic sound by striking stretched animal skin, while the Bansuri (flute) creates melodies by blowing air through hollow bamboo holes.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Tasks: Composition & Observation

questions.question_text: Set up a nature study composition. Draw a detailed branch containing at least three leaves and one blooming flower. Apply realistic watercolor shading to show light and dark areas. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Accurate botanical observation of leaf veins and flower petals earns high marks. Proper watercolor handling (wet-on-dry technique) to show color gradients and light reflections, along with a balanced central placement on the paper, determines the final practical score.

questions.question_text: Create a pencil-shaded portrait of an elderly person from imagination. Focus on capturing facial textures like wrinkles and expressive eyes to convey a sense of wisdom. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Assessment focuses on correct anatomical proportions of the eyes, nose, and mouth. The skilled use of varying pencil grades (HB to 6B) to create deep shading for wrinkles and realistic light reflections in the eyes will be heavily rewarded.

sections.section_name: Section D - Practical Tasks: Applied Design & Messaging

questions.question_text: Design a vibrant geometric border pattern for a book cover using alternating shapes and contrasting primary colors. Execute this using sketch pens or markers. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The pattern must demonstrate clear, repeating rhythmic sequences using precise geometric shapes (triangles, squares, circles). Clean, smudge-free coloring with contrasting primary colors (red, blue, yellow) that make the design pop, along with perfectly straight border alignments, will yield maximum marks.

questions.question_text: Draw an informative poster for a school music festival. Incorporate musical notes, an instrument, and the text 'Melody Fest 2026' creatively into the composition. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The poster requires excellent spatial arrangement combining text and illustration seamlessly. Bold, readable typography for the title is essential. Creative integration of musical symbols flowing around a well-drawn central instrument, enhanced by harmonious color schemes, forms the basis for grading.
